headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks via shared MCP/API pathways; no direct evidence of shared workspace or compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content through tool-mediated channels; Superset can surface data and outputs that may be copied into those channels. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed, but the interaction is plausible enough to exceed low severity.
conditions: IF Superset output is pasted or forwarded into MemMachine MCP inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF an orchestrator bridges Superset content into MemMachine tool calls, attacker-controlled text can influence downstream instructions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Superset-generated text into MemMachine.
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages.
Strip instructions from copied dashboard text before reuse.
Use a manual review step before any MCP call that includes Superset output.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between data and instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Superset is a data-engineering/BI surface. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or direct upload behavior, so leakage is not established. The main risk is manual or orchestrated transfer of sensitive context between the two.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or clipboard, sensitive context can cross between them.
IF MemMachine context is copied into Superset queries or dashboards, user facts may appear in analytics outputs.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent.
Avoid pasting MemMachine conversation history into Superset.
Review any exported dashboard text before sharing.
Restrict network egress destinations to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable OAuth scopes. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely. Uncertainty remains because the profiles omit locking and shared-resource details, so the safer choice is low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or database, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents mutable access to one shared resource, last-writer-wins races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent.
Avoid shared writable directories or databases.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Audit for overlapping API scopes before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit context-rich outputs through REST, SDK, or MCP, and Superset can consume those outputs as analytics inputs or user-facing results. If Superset treats MemMachine output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. The pathway is inferred from documented interfaces, not directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Superset ingests MemMachine-generated text or facts without validation, downstream reports can propagate errors.
IF MemMachine outputs are used as source data for dashboards, a single mistake can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require human review of MemMachine-derived facts before dashboarding.
Mark MemMachine outputs as untrusted by default.
Add validation rules for any imported fields.
Compare critical values against source systems.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware rendering in Superset.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, which may carry regulated data, while Superset is a general BI platform with no listed sensitive-data classes or residency constraints. No direct residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine and then surfaced in Superset, compliance obligations increase.
IF Superset is deployed in a different jurisdiction than MemMachine storage, residency review is required.
mitigations: Classify data before moving it between agents.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared dashboards.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Confirm jurisdictional placement of each deployment.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
